open.playerName: Cam Little and the Jaguars D/ST

Little at 146.1 season is the highest-projected kicker available to this roster - ahead of Cairo Santos 143.2, Boswell 142.1 and Reichard 141.8 - and returned 12.0 in week 1. The Jaguars D/ST returned 12.0 with five sacks and rank 4th for week 2 despite the Denver draw, above Baltimore's 5th, which is the opposite of what seasonProj says (Baltimore 125.7, Jacksonville 103.9). Taking the week 2 rankings over the season field. Both are waiver claims here and priority never resets, so a stream would have to clear a much higher bar than a projection gap. REVIEWED 15 Sep: BOTH HELD, now on Week 2 boards rather than season fields. FantasyPros Week 2 has Cam Little K8 (Loop K2, Santos K4, McLaughlin K7, Pineiro K9, Boswell K15); Little returned 12.0 in Week 1. Lindy's Week 2 D/ST board has Jacksonville 9th and Baltimore 2nd - so unlike Chem, where Baltimore was claimed this morning, the answer here is still hold, and the reason is priority rather than the ranking. Both upgrades were explicitly declined and published as watch or doNotChase rows so a future run does not rediscover them as new.

open.thesis: Declined the best player on this wire on purpose, and recorded it so a future run does not 'discover' him. Coker went 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores in Week 1 - 36.8 points, the top receiver in the NFL - and the Monday walking boot is precautionary by his own account with a Wednesday practice expected. He is being CLAIMED in Chem this morning, where priority resets weekly and it is free. Here it is declined because IPADE priority never resets, we are 5th of 10, and he would not start: the receiver slots are Rashee Rice and Garrett Wilson and the flex has Tuten. The standing rule is that priority buys an immediate starter or a league-winner, and a bench stash is neither. Same player, same evidence, opposite answer, and the only variable is the waiver rule.
open.falsifiedIf: Garrett Wilson or Rashee Rice is ruled out for a multi-week stretch, or Coker posts a second week above 25 points while still unrostered in this league - either makes him a starter, and a starter is what priority is for.

open.thesis: Keep Tuten in the RB/WR/TE flex over MarShawn Lloyd despite Lloyd projecting 11.6 to Tuten's 9.4. This is the reverse of the Chem call in the same week and the reason is evidence quality, not scoring. Tuten's Week 1 is confirmed - 48% of snaps, 16 touches, most on the Jacksonville offence, 88 yards. Lloyd's role is well sourced (Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list indefinitely, Yahoo's read is roughly twenty touches a game and about a month of starts) but his actual Week 1 snap share could NOT be confirmed: the packers.com game notes returned by search were dated 22 August, preseason. Swapping a confirmed 16-touch lead back for an unconfirmed one on a 2.2-point projection edge is the pattern the churn rule exists to stop. Flagged in the run report as the call most likely to be wrong.

Worth generalising: a FREEAGENT tag on a player whose team has not yet played is an artifact, not an opportunity.
